findings.title: No `**Commit**:` markers in a 16-task slice file
findings.description: The task file is a 16-task breakdown with no `**Commit**:` markers anywhere. While the instructions say a file with no markers is acceptable in principle, a slice this size produces numerous working, tested points (each implementation task is followed immediately by its test task) that should be checkpointed with commits. The CLAUDE.md git rules require "git add and commit from project root at least once per task." With 16 tasks and no commit markers at all, the breakdown does not guide the implementing agent toward the natural commit boundaries (after each implementation-plus-test pair). For a slice with this many independently testable units, the absence of any commit guidance is a proportionality gap: not a FAIL because markers are optional, but a CONCERN because the slice is large enough that committing only at the end would produce a single enormous commit, and the project conventions explicitly say to commit at least once per task.

findings.title: Every functional success criterion traces to a concrete task
findings.description:
Each functional success criterion from the slice design has a corresponding task:
- Slice branch body (design, checked/unchecked items, review provenance): Task 11 (section contract), Task 7 (inputs), Task 9 (assembly).
- Non-slice branch with three no-input lines: Task 11.2 (unplanned repository case), Task 16.2 step 4 (live walkthrough).
- Merged ancestor excluded → no-input provenance: Task 8.2 (load-bearing ancestor case).
- Integration branch absent from host → fail naming branch: Task 5.1/5.2 (D1 table), Task 16.2 step 2 (live).
- Integration branch present → base with source: Task 5.1/5.2.
- Unpushed/behind branch → push command: Task 6.1/6.2, Task 16.2 step 3.
- Missing section → fail, create nothing: Task 12.1/12.2, Task 13.2.
- Title terms and fallback: Task 10a.1/10a.2.
- Dry-run/real equality: Task 13.1/13.2, Task 16.2 step 5.
- Operator identification failure: Task 13.2 (identity refusal case), Task 14.1 (failure matrix includes `identify_operator`).
- One recorded live creation: Task 16.2/16.3.

No functional criterion is left without a task.

findings.title: Every technical success criterion traces to a concrete task
findings.description:
Each technical success criterion has a corresponding task:
- Timeout constants (`HOST_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` for gh, `GIT_QUERY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` for ls-remote) and scripted timeout at five call sites: Task 14.1, explicitly referencing F007/D2.
- Provider failure during composition → non-zero exit, ERROR log, nothing created: Task 10.1/10.2, Task 14 covers the model call's boundary failure.
- Default path makes exactly one host write, only after every read: Task 13.1 (ordering) and 13.2 (happy-path one write).
- `review/` does not import `pr/`, asserted by import-boundary test: Task 15.1.
- Checkbox parser handles nested, `[x]`/`[X]`, trailing whitespace, with real-file fixture: Task 2.1/2.2.
- `pyright` zero errors, `ruff` clean: Task 16.1.
- `summary_oneshot` docstring correction with test: Task 15.2.

No technical criterion is unmet.

findings.title: Task sequencing respects dependencies with no circular dependencies
findings.description:
The task order follows the design's "Implementation Notes → Order" exactly:
- Tasks 1–2 (parsers) have no dependencies — correct as the first tasks.
- Task 3 (git helpers) depends on nothing new — placed before its consumers (Tasks 7, 8).
- Task 4 (`resolve_locator`) is independent — correctly placed before Task 13 which consumes it.
- Tasks 5–6 (base, preconditions) depend on 381 and Task 3 — both already done.
- Tasks 7–8 (inputs) depend on Tasks 1, 2, 3 — all precede them.
- Task 9 (assembly) depends on Task 7–8 data shapes.
- Tasks 10, 10a, 11, 12 (body) depend on Task 9.
- Task 13 (command) depends on all prior.
- Task 14 (failure matrix) depends on Task 13 wiring — correctly follows.
- Task 15 (guard, docstring) is independent of the command; correctly last-before-verification.
- Task 16 (verification) is last.
No task references a later task as a prerequisite; no circular dependencies.

findings.title: Test tasks immediately follow their implementation tasks (test-with pattern)
findings.description:
Every implementation task is immediately followed by its test task:
- 1.1 → 1.2, 2.1 → 2.2, 3.1 → 3.2, 4.1 → 4.2, 5.1 → 5.2, 6.1 → 6.2, 7.1 → 7.2, 8.1 → 8.2, 9.1 → 9.2, 10.1 → 10.2, 10a.1 → 10a.2, 11.1 → 11.2, 12.1 → 12.2, 13.1 → 13.2.
- Task 14 (failure matrix) is test-only by design — it tests the command wired in Task 13 and all five host calls; it has no separate implementation subtask because the implementation is the error handling in Task 13/10/6, and the matrix is explicitly modeled on 384's test-only Task 7. This is consistent, not a gap.
The test-with pattern is uniformly applied.

findings.title: Task granularity is appropriate — no tasks too large or too granular
findings.description: Task effort estimates range from 1 to 3, with most at 2. No single task exceeds effort 3. Tasks are scoped to single responsibilities (one parser, one helper set, one design decision). The body layer (Tasks 10, 10a, 11, 12) is split by concern (composer, title, section contract, presence check) rather than bundled into one monolith — this is appropriate given each has distinct failure modes and test cases. Tasks are independently completable by a junior AI: each has clear file targets, explicit success criteria, and specific test cases. No task is too granular (no task is just a single trivial line) or too large (no task spans multiple unrelated modules).

findings.title: No scope creep — every task traces to a design decision or success criterion
findings.description:
Every task cites its design decision (D1–D8, D4a) or success criterion. The Context Summary explicitly justifies each task's inclusion:
- Tasks 1–2 are new parsers the tree lacks, explicitly motivated.
- Task 4 (`resolve_locator` extraction) is D6 — shared prefix extraction, not new logic.
- Task 15 (docstring correction) is D3's "correction owed" — explicitly stated as owed by the design.
- Task 14 mirrors 384's Task 7 matrix — directly from the technical success criterion on timeouts.
No task introduces functionality outside the slice's included scope. The excluded list (pushing, editing PRs, draft PRs, reviewers, labels, cross-repo, posting review, slash command) is respected — no task touches any excluded item.
